title: Part
summary: The basic 3D building block: a primitive block/sphere/cylinder with physics, position, size, color, and the Touched event. Almost everything physical starts as a Part.

properties.name: Position
properties.description: Center of the part in world coordinates. Use for measurements.

properties.name: CFrame
properties.description: Position AND orientation. Use for placement/movement.

properties.name: Anchored
properties.description: true = physics frozen in place (buildings, floors). false = simulated (falls, pushed).

properties.name: CanCollide
properties.description: Whether physical collisions occur with this part.

properties.name: CanTouch
properties.description: Whether Touched events can fire for this part.

properties.name: Transparency
properties.description: 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible). Note: 1 does NOT disable collision.

properties.name: Mass / AssemblyLinearVelocity
properties.description: Computed mass; velocity of the assembly the part belongs to.

events.name: Touched
events.description: Fires when another part begins touching this one. Passes the OTHER part. Requires CanTouch on both and actual physics contact.

explanation.whatItIs: The atom of Roblox worlds: a physical box (or sphere/cylinder via Shape) you can place, color, anchor, collide with, and touch.
explanation.whyItExists: Every 3D game needs primitives with physics. Parts are those primitives, plus the hooks (Touched) that make gameplay happen.
whenToUse: Kill bricks, pads, triggers via Touched + attributes/tags
whenNotToUse: Pure visual-only decor at scale — consider merged meshes for performance
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
Part = box + physics + appearance
  Anchored=true   → statue (stays put)
  Anchored=false  → object (falls, pushes)
  CanCollide      → can I bump it?
  CanTouch+Touched → can it notice me?
```
tips: Touched fires PER touching part — a character can fire it 5+ times; debounce or check for humanoid
Invisible ≠ non-colliding: set CanCollide=false for ghost blocks
Move parts with CFrame (PivotTo/CFrame math), not Position, when orientation matters
Set CanQuery/CanCollide deliberately for trigger volumes
commonMistakes: Trusting one Touched event per person — limbs trigger multiple touches
Unanchoring a part you meant to stay (watch it fall at runtime)
Comparing Positions for movement instead of using CFrame
Making invisible walls but forgetting CanCollide — players walk through

examples.title: Kill brick (the classic)
examples.code:
local killBrick = script.Parent

killBrick.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
    local humanoid = hit.Parent:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
    if humanoid then
        humanoid.Health = 0
    end
end)
examples.commonMistake: No debounce here is fine (setting Health=0 is idempotent), but for rewards you MUST guard against multiple touches.

examples.title: A bouncy pad
examples.code:
local pad = script.Parent

pad.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
    local root = hit.Parent:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
    if root then
        root.AssemblyLinearVelocity = Vector3.new(0, 100, 0)
    end
end)
